name: SCHARE Smart Devices and Sensing Technologies Grand Challenge (Phase I)
org: National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities (NIMHD), NIH
why: NIH challenge that explicitly asks for wearable sensors, software and integrated sensing ecosystems that generate interoperable, AI-ready whole-person data. Phase I only asks for a proof of concept, so a pre-launch team with a nightly personal-baseline concept and a developer SDK can enter. Free, fully online (web form plus a Box upload). Eligibility: US citizen team lead or a US-incorporated entity; SAM.gov entity setup is needed to receive any cash award.
why_now: Launched 21 Sep 2026; sign-up closes 18 Dec 2026; Phase I proof of concept due 15 Feb 2027; Phase I winners named 26 Mar 2027.
channel: Online sign-up form linked from the challenge page, then submission to an assigned Box folder; questions to the published SCHARE challenges inbox (SCHAREChallenges@nih.gov)
warm_path: None known. Cold: the challenge inbox, and the NIH SCHARE Think-a-Thon community listed on the same site.
ask: Sign up by 18 Dec 2026 and send a Phase I proof of concept by 15 Feb 2027 for the nightly personal-baseline data layer and SDK as an interoperable research data source.
opener: Hello SCHARE team, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh, NC. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK that gives researchers consistent nightly data. We plan to enter Phase I with a proof of concept for an interoperable, AI ready nightly data layer that could sit alongside SCHARE. We have not launched yet, we have a public waitlist, and we are veteran, woman and minority owned. Could we confirm scope fit on a short call before we submit? https://calendly.com/jeremy-vybe/30min
geo: US (online; US citizen lead or US-incorporated entity)

name: ST Innovation Challenge (healthcare and wearables track, Innovation World Cup 2027)
org: STMicroelectronics with the Innovation World Cup Series (Techpreneurs)
why: STMicroelectronics' flagship startup programme for hardware teams; its scope names healthcare and wearables (biosignal sensing, wellness devices, body-worn electronics that process data on device). Taking part means free ST development kits such as SensorTile.box PRO, work with ST field application engineers and business advice, all remote. Entry is free. Fits a band plus SDK team that wants silicon and edge AI support from a big chip maker.

name: Military Founders Lab, cohort 27A (Ideation/Seed track)
org: D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families (IVMF), Syracuse University (Bunker Labs legacy)
why: Free, fully online 10-week founder programme for veterans and military spouses, the successor to Bunker Labs programming. Its Ideation/Seed track is built for pre-revenue businesses with capital invested, which fits pre-launch Vybe. Weekly live Founders Exchange with peer founders plus expert sessions; about 5 to 8 hours a week. Requirements on its own page: honourable service documentation, a registered business, 6+ months of active development, under 250K revenue or capital invested.

name: AgeTech Collaborative January Open Mic Challenge, accelerator and Testbed network
why: Exploratory testbed route. AARP's nonprofit AgeTech Collaborative runs an online Open Mic pitch event; being selected makes a startup eligible for its 8-week virtual accelerator (no cost, no equity), and graduates are connected to its Testbed network of senior living, hospital and university partners to pilot with real older adult users. A nightly heart rate, HRV and sleep timing baseline fits the 50+ healthy-ageing market.
why_now: January Open Mic Challenge is an online event on 28 Jan 2027; applications close 31 Oct 2026, 11:59 pm.
channel: Online pitch application on the events page
warm_path: None known. Cold via the application; AARP research staff speak at the accelerator info sessions listed on the events page.
ask: Apply by 31 Oct 2026 to pitch at the 28 Jan 2027 online Open Mic, with the goal of entering the accelerator and then a Testbed pilot with older adult users.
opener: I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh, NC. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, so adults 50 and over can see how their nights change over time without another screen. A developer SDK lets care and wellness apps use the same nightly signals. We have not launched yet, we have a public waitlist, and we are veteran, woman and minority owned. We would welcome the chance to pitch and to learn from AARP's testbed partners. https://calendly.com/jeremy-vybe/30min
